site.name: Barker No. 1 Mine
site.location: Boulder County Tungsten District / Clark Tunnel
overview: Barker No. 1 was a historic tungsten mine developed from the Clark Tunnel in the Boulder County Tungsten District.
Colorado's 1960 tungsten-mine inventory places the Barker No. 1 workings about 200 feet inside the Clark Tunnel and records two working levels with historic tungsten production.
moreHistory: The state mine inventory estimates Barker No. 1 production at roughly 2,000 to 3,000 tungsten units and describes ore stopes above and below the Clark Tunnel level. U.S. Geological Survey work also describes the Barker No. 1 vein as a continuation of the Vasco No. 8 vein.

The coordinate used here is a documented Barker Mine / Clark Tunnel locality-level anchor near 39.97027, -105.48083. It identifies the historic mine area without claiming that Remnant has field-surveyed a surviving portal, shaft collar, or underground working.
A focused exact-site media search did not locate a defensible reusable Barker No. 1 image, so nearby tungsten-district photographs were rejected rather than attached to the wrong mine.
